chapter: George Shearing and becoming a manager
title: Big bands in decline in the early 1950s
summary: Big bands struggled after the war; Basie dropped to six pieces while small groups like Shearing and Brubeck thrived on colleges.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: And were you like aware of, I mean the big bands were still out there although it was —
They were still out there but they were—
It was after the war kind of —
Yeah, they were kind of down. They were having a hard time, a very difficult time.
And like what was the status—

That was the time when Basie finally broke up and had the six pieces, you know, because it was really rough out there for big bands. But groups like George was really hot, and Dave Brubeck, and that was the hottest things going, playing the colleges and you know, so it was really — the big band it just cost too much to travel. And the economics of it at that time was even worse than they are now. I mean they’re bad enough now, but for a big band it was terrible, you know.
